content.title: About
content.content: Pretzels are a baked snack shaped into twisted knots, traditionally made from wheat flour, water, salt, and yeast. They feature a crunchy crust and a soft, slightly chewy interior. Pretzels are often sprinkled with coarse salt and may be flavored with seeds, cheese, or spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels originated in medieval Europe and were originally a symbol of crossed arms, meaning “peace”.
The traditional German “Brezel” has a double‑knot shape symbolizing two hands crossed in prayer.
Pretzel popularity in the United States surged in the early 20th century thanks to German immigrants.
There are sweet pretzel varieties coated with sugar glaze or chocolate.
In some countries, such as Switzerland, pretzels are served with mustard dip.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pretzels contain starch, providing a steady release of energy.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many snack foods, traditional pretzels contain virtually no fat.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The wheat flour used in pretzels supplies iron, essential for blood formation.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 supports protein metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain pretzel versions are rich in fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Pretzels are made from wheat flour, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because of their high starch content, pretzels can raise blood sugar quickly.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Traditional pretzels are often heavily salted, which may be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although low in fat, the carbohydrate load makes pretzels relatively calorie‑dense when eaten in large portions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, served with dips (mustard, cheese, creamy spreads), or incorporated into dishes such as salads, soups, and snack platters. They are commonly paired with beer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry pretzels in an airtight container at room temperature, away from moisture. They can be frozen for longer shelf life and reheated in the oven to restore crispness before serving.
